messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 — model-serving-queue growth detected. queue length > 12k, sustained 3m. autoscaler attempted scale but failures reported. paging on-call.

maria: On it. seeing a huge spike in model-serving queue. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/model-serving/queue

liam: hitting this now too — `kubectl get pods -n model-serving` shows ~120 Pending, reason: 0/0 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient gpu.

maria: autoscaler logs show repeated create-instance errors: `CreateFleetInstances failed: InvalidInstanceProfile: InstanceProfile gpu-node-role-v2 does not exist`

liam: that explains it. we rolled new launch-template last night for improved AMI. looks like the instance profile name changed and ASG/launch config refers to it. autoscaler tries to create nodes but AWS returns InvalidInstanceProfile, so no nodes are coming up.

maria: quick mitigation — can we manually set desired capacity on the ASG to provision warm CPU nodes (no GPUs) to drain backlog? some inference routes can fallback to CPU models.

jordan: We have two concerns: 1) immediate queue growth/customer impact 2) permanently broken LT rollout process. For now, manual ASG scale won't help if launch template is invalid. we need to either (A) rollback LT to previous template id or (B) fix IAM instance profile name. which is faster?

liam: rollback is fastest. console -> ASG -> edit launch template to previous version. I'll do the rollback, need someone in AWS console with perm to update.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook: GPU-Autoscale-LT-Failure v2. Steps: 1) Confirm error in autoscaler logs. 2) Check AWS ASG/LaunchTemplate version. 3) Rollback LT OR update instance profile. 4) Monitor node registration. 5) If customers impacted, open support case and route to comms.

maria: I'm on the console now, rolling LT back to v42 -> v41. bookmarking commands: `aws ec2 describe-launch-templates --launch-template-ids lt-0abcde1234` then `aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-id lt-0abcde1234 --default-version 41`

liam: after rollback, autoscaler produced a couple create attempts and we see EC2 instances launching. however new nodes are registering with taint `node.kubernetes.io/gpu-untrusted:NoSchedule`. pods still pending because they tolerate gpu taint? checking pod tolerations...

maria: pods don't have the toleration, our addon that auto-applies tolerations to `model-serving` namespace recently changed in the operator upgrade. that operator upgrade also changed default toleration logic. ops.

jordan: so two cascading failures: launch-template->IAM profile mismatch prevented node creation, then operator change removed tolerations so even when nodes appear they won't host model-serving pods. we need to add toleration to the replicasets or revert operator.

liam: quick patch: `kubectl patch deploy -n model-serving model-api -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"node.kubernetes.io/gpu-untrusted","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'` will let the existing pods schedule. doing that now.

maria: patch applied. pods are moving to ContainerCreating -> Running. queue drain started. latency for hosted API dropping from 12s -> 1.6s for routed CPU fallbacks; GPU-backed requests still queued but draining.

sam: thanks team — I'm taking handoff for the next shift. summary: root cause rollback-in-flight changed instance profile name in launch template, autoscaler couldn't create GPU nodes. concurrent operator change removed tolerations causing scheduling failures. immediate mitigations: rolled LT back, patched deployments with toleration, scaled down low-priority batch jobs.

jordan: customer impact note: several mid-sized customers experienced 5–12 minute increased tail latency and occasional 502s while requests retried. no data loss; requests queued and served when capacity recovered. filing incident report.

maria: actions assigned: @jordan -> post-incident: reconcile LT rollout process and add CI guard against instance profile mismatches. @liam -> revert the operator change or fix operator config to reintroduce tolerations permanently. @sam -> monitor queues and coord comms with support.

sre-runbook-bot: Handoff checklist completed. Handoff to @sam at 23:02 UTC.

sam: I'll monitor for the next 2 hours and then reassign to weekday oncall. thumbs if you saw the rollback. :thumbsup:

liam: :thumbsup: adding a short-term alert around launch-template-default-version changes and a preflight check to confirm instance profile exists.

maria: note for postmortem: decouple operator upgrades from LT rollouts in the same release window. also add a staged rollout for toleration/operator change.

jordan: logging note: captured autoscaler error fragments and ASG event history. attaching to incident ticket.

sam: thanks all. closing page for now — reopening if queue grows again. :white_check_mark:
